name: fuel_type:seats
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible: large-seat diesel/petrol vehicles (minibuses, MPVs) have different claim profiles from small-seat electric vehicles. Recommend checking cell credibility for rare combinations (e.g., electric + 8 seats) and applying smoothing or collapsing sparse cells.

name: vehicle_brand:fuel_type

Credibility concern for sparse brand x fuel_type cells — recommend grouping low-volume brand/fuel combinations and applying shrinkage. Regulatorily defensible as it reflects objective vehicle characteristics.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:seats
actuary_note: Actuarially sound: a high power-to-weight ratio in a 7-seat vehicle implies different usage and accident dynamics than the same ratio in a 2-seat sports car. Recommend banding both variables before interaction to ensure cell credibility.

name: bonus_score:business_type
actuary_note: Actuarially well-motivated: bonus score is a stronger individual risk signal for private than commercial business. Regulatorily defensible as it reflects genuine differences in how claims history translates to future risk by business type.

name: bonus_score:liability_exposure
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible from an adverse selection perspective. Recommend validating with observed loss ratios in the high bonus_score x high liability_exposure cell. If the interaction is confirmed empirically, it is regulatorily defensible as it reflects objective risk characteristics.

name: payment_frequency:policy_type
actuary_note: Partially actuarial, partially commercial. The interaction is defensible if instalment loadings genuinely differ by policy type, or if lapse/cancellation risk (which affects earned premium) varies by this combination. Recommend confirming with lapse and cancellation data segmented by policy_type x payment_frequency.

name: bonus_score:municipality_type
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible: the bonus score is a stronger discriminator in rural areas where individual driving behaviour dominates, versus urban areas where environmental risk is the primary driver. Regulatorily defensible as both factors are objective risk characteristics.

name: seats:municipality_type
actuary_note: Actuarially reasonable. Recommend validating with frequency data segmented by seats band and municipality_type. Cell credibility may be a concern for high seat counts in rural areas — apply smoothing as needed.

name: bonus_score:payment_frequency
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible as a behavioural risk proxy. However, regulators may scrutinise payment_frequency as a socioeconomic proxy. Recommend ensuring the interaction is supported by empirical loss ratio evidence and is not acting as a proxy for protected characteristics. Document the actuarial justification carefully.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:fuel_type
actuary_note: Actuarially justified given the distinct performance characteristics of EVs vs. ICE vehicles at equivalent power-to-weight ratios. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective vehicle characteristics. Recommend monitoring as EV data volume grows.

name: vehicle_value:bonus_score
actuary_note: Actuarially sound: a poor bonus score driver in a high-value vehicle is a materially different risk than the same driver in a low-value vehicle. Recommend validating with observed severity data segmented by vehicle_value band and bonus_score band.

name: vehicle_value:policy_type
actuary_note: Strongly actuarially justified: vehicle value should have near-zero effect for TPONLY policies and maximum effect for comprehensive. This interaction is structurally important and regulatorily defensible. Recommend confirming the expected pattern in the data.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:vehicle_brand
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible but introduces complexity. Credibility concern for brand x power_to_weight_ratio cells. Recommend banding power_to_weight_ratio and grouping brands before fitting. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective vehicle characteristics.

name: bonus_score:policy_type
actuary_note: Actuarially justified: the bonus score interacts with the scope of cover to determine total expected loss. Regulatorily defensible. Recommend validating the interaction pattern against observed loss ratios by policy_type x bonus_score band.

name: bonus_score:driver_age
actuary_note: Actuarially well-motivated: a poor bonus score at age 20 has different implications than at age 50. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective risk characteristics. Recommend banding driver_age and bonus_score for GLM implementation.

name: bonus_score:age_driving_licence
actuary_note: Actuarially sound and regulatorily defensible. Note potential collinearity with driver_age x bonus_score interaction — recommend assessing whether both interactions are needed simultaneously or if one subsumes the other. Consider model parsimony.

name: policy_type:municipality_type
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible. Recommend validating with frequency data by policy_type x municipality_type. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective risk characteristics.

name: vehicle_brand:seats
actuary_note: Actuarially reasonable but introduces complexity. Credibility concern for rare brand x seat count combinations. Recommend collapsing brands into groups and banding seats before fitting. Consider whether this interaction adds materially over the main effects given the vehicle_brand:fuel_type interaction already included.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:age_driving_licence
actuary_note: Actuarially well-justified: the risk of high-performance vehicles is substantially higher for inexperienced drivers. Regulatorily defensible. Recommend banding both variables for GLM implementation and validating with frequency data.

name: power_to_weight_ratio:policy_type
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible. Recommend confirming the interaction pattern is not driven by selection effects (high-performance vehicles rarely being TPONLY). If cell volumes are low for high power_to_weight_ratio x TPONLY, consider constraining the interaction.

name: policy_type:circulation_area
actuary_note: Actuarially justified. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective risk characteristics. Recommend validating the interaction pattern with frequency and severity data by policy_type x circulation_area.

name: liability_exposure:age_driving_licence
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible. Recommend validating with claims data to confirm the direction and magnitude of the interaction. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective risk characteristics.

name: seats:circulation_area
actuary_note: Actuarially reasonable. Recommend validating with frequency data. Cell credibility may be a concern for high seat counts in certain circulation areas — apply smoothing as needed.

name: vehicle_value:payment_frequency
actuary_note: Partially actuarial, partially commercial. Regulators may scrutinise payment_frequency as a socioeconomic proxy. Recommend ensuring empirical loss ratio support and documenting that the interaction reflects genuine risk differentiation rather than socioeconomic proxying. Lower priority than other interactions — include only if empirically validated.

name: vehicle_value:fuel_type
actuary_note: Actuarially justified given the distinct repair cost structures of EVs. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective vehicle characteristics. Recommend monitoring as EV repair cost data matures.

name: vehicle_value:power_to_weight_ratio
actuary_note: Actuarially sound. Recommend banding both variables for GLM implementation. Consider whether this interaction adds materially over the vehicle_value main effect and power_to_weight_ratio main effect given other interactions already included.

name: payment_frequency:driver_age
actuary_note: Regulators may scrutinise this interaction as payment_frequency could act as a socioeconomic proxy, particularly for young drivers. Recommend strong empirical validation and careful documentation. Include only if loss ratio evidence clearly supports the interaction beyond the main effects.

name: vehicle_age:policy_type
actuary_note: Actuarially well-justified: vehicle age affects own-damage severity and total loss probability, which is only relevant for comprehensive cover. Regulatorily defensible. Recommend validating the interaction pattern with claims data.

name: vehicle_age:business_type
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible. Recommend validating with frequency and severity data segmented by vehicle_age band and business_type. Regulatorily defensible as both are objective risk characteristics.

name: seats:age_driving_licence
actuary_note: Actuarially reasonable. Recommend banding both variables and validating with frequency data. Consider model parsimony — this interaction may be partially captured by the power_to_weight_ratio:age_driving_licence interaction already included.

name: driver_age:seats
actuary_note: Actuarially plausible. Recommend validating with frequency data. Consider whether this adds materially over the seats main effect and driver_age main effect given other driver-age interactions already included. Apply parsimony principle.
